overview: Preserve the imported effective 2D QWP source model as a clearly identified reference. Its own real amplitude symbols and phase parameters remain distinct from the general crystal library. The matrix-chain output is compared with an independent closed-form source intensity, rather than substituting that closed form for the production calculation.
workflow: Declare the source-specific real parameters and complex 2D tensor.
Run the original QWP chain and resolve circular scattering amplitudes.
Rebuild the analyzer reference axis and phase factors.
Retain independently derived intensity terms for validation, then validate source input values.

blocks.title: Define the effective source tensor and workflow identifiers
blocks.explanation: Declare separate real a,A,δ,φ symbols. Build R=[[a,A*exp(i*δ)],[-A*exp(i*δ),a*exp(i*φ)]], name the source mode and map internal workflow/model identifiers to readable labels. The off-diagonal signs are those of this imported effective model.
blocks.why: Reusing the general complex a symbol would change the source algebra assumptions. The source antisymmetric off-diagonal pair also must not be silently imposed on a nonmagnetic symmetric D2h material tensor.
blocks.check: At φ=0 the diagonal entries coincide. At A=0 the model becomes diagonal. This source model has no crystal-surface parameter.

blocks.title: qwp_source_algebra: cache the fixed symbolic calculation
blocks.explanation: lru_cache(maxsize=1) stores this parameter-independent symbolic result after its first evaluation. Build the QWP optical chain, call the same transverse amplitude engine and calculate R++=<σ⁺|R|σ⁺> and R-+=<σ⁻|R|σ⁺>.
blocks.why: The symbolic source structure is fixed; repeatedly rebuilding it for every numerical slider value would waste time. Numerical coefficient values are substituted after retrieving this symbolic record.
blocks.check: The source record amplitude comes from the actual matrix chain. Cached expressions remain symbolic in the four real source parameters.

blocks.title: Reconstruct the source analyzer reference and relative phase
blocks.explanation: Pass both circular basis states through the return QWP. Remove a global phase from the dominant σ⁺ output component to construct a real reference axis, rotate that axis by +90 degrees, project the σ⁻ output onto the perpendicular axis and build the scanned analyzer. Check it against the optical_chain analyzer.
blocks.why: The angle zero and phase ratio determine the interference sign. An analyzer measured from laboratory X is not automatically the same convention as an analyzer measured from the returned σ⁺ axis.
blocks.check: The source reference is +Y, its perpendicular direction is -X and the reconstructed analyzer equals (-sin(α),cos(α)).

blocks.title: Compute circular-channel powers and their interference
blocks.explanation: Calculate |R++|^2, |R-+|^2 and Im(R++*R-+.conjugate()) directly from the symbolic circular amplitudes using the real source parameter assumptions.
blocks.why: In this adopted return-optic chain, the relative QWP phase turns the analyzer interference coefficient into the imaginary part of the circular-amplitude product.
blocks.check: These independently computed terms must agree with the source formulas built in the next block.

blocks.title: Build an independent closed-form source reference
blocks.explanation: Construct reference_pp=a^2*cos(φ/2)^2+A^2+2aA*cos(φ/2)*sin(φ/2-δ), reference_mp=a^2*sin(φ/2)^2 and the corresponding cross coefficient. Form the source intensity as reference_pp*cos(α)^2+reference_mp*sin(α)^2+2*reference_cross*sin(α)*cos(α).
blocks.why: A separately stated analytic law provides a useful regression target. It is retained for checks and reporting while the production amplitude still comes from matrix multiplication.
blocks.check: With φ=0, R-+ vanishes. With A=0 the result reduces to a^2*cos(α-φ/2)^2 in the adopted convention.

blocks.title: Return all source intermediates
blocks.explanation: Return the production record, circular amplitudes, returned circular vectors, phase factors, analyzer axes, directly calculated powers and independent source intensity pieces in one dictionary.
blocks.why: A calculation can be inspected stage by stage rather than judged only by its final polar curve.
blocks.check: Reports should identify whether a value is a production matrix result or an independent source reference; neither may be mixed with the slide-specific component prescription.

blocks.title: qwp_source_values: validate and substitute source parameters
blocks.explanation: Require a,A,delta_deg,phi_deg, validate each as a finite real number and convert the input decimals to rationals. Map the two amplitudes to their source symbols and convert phase degrees to radians.
blocks.why: The imported source makes the amplitudes real and locates complex character in explicit phases. Its substitution dictionary must use those same symbols and units.
blocks.check: An incomplete parameter dictionary raises an error. A 90-degree δ substitutes π/2, not the number 90 inside exp(i*δ).

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–7 in order and confirm the Cell 07/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: This effective 2D tensor is a retained source model, not a symmetry certificate for CaNb2O6.
The alternative convention in the source appendix is not silently substituted for the adopted main chain.
The cached symbolic expressions must be evaluated with source parameters, not the general crystal coefficient dictionary.
A 3D material extension preserves the chosen QWP optical sequence while supplying a rotated symmetry-allowed crystal tensor.

overview: Attach reference conventions, illustrative material examples and conditional circular selection diagnostics to the existing engine. The complex-linear reference supplies phase-sensitive VV/VH examples; the circular-selection reference supplies necessary angular-momentum congruences with stated scope. These congruences do not predict a quantitative vortex-beam intensity.
workflow: Record reference roles and extend the material library.
Build explicit linear and circular demonstration configurations.
Validate integer selection-rule controls and transform tensors into the circular basis.
Report plane-wave channels and conditional selection checks separately.
Offer a supplied-term resonance utility without inferring microscopic parameters.

blocks.title: Identify the scan symbol and reference roles
blocks.explanation: Declare θ as a real display symbol. PAPER_SOURCES records the two reference titles, DOIs, relevant equation ranges and documented scope, then merges them into SOURCES. The calculation still uses the explicit state and tensor definitions; citation metadata does not choose the optical method.
blocks.why: A linear-polarization intensity formalism and an angular-momentum selection rule answer different questions. The program must not promote a necessary circular rule into a universal quantitative scattering law.
blocks.check: The circular source role points to DOI 10.1039/D1CP02209A, while complex-linear scans point to DOI 10.1039/D1CP03626B.

blocks.title: Extend the library with black phosphorus
blocks.explanation: Add a D2h example with layer plane xz, surface normal y and separate Ag(1),B2g,Ag(2) branches. The lattice is a unity principal-plane reference; the dedicated reference factory below supplies the printed coefficient ratios.
blocks.why: The same group label D2h can use an axis setting different from an intuitive xy layer drawing. The axes must match the equations being reproduced.
blocks.check: The chosen (010) geometry projects the xz tensor subspace. The two Ag branches retain independent coefficient dictionaries.

blocks.title: Extend the library with monolayer MoS2
blocks.explanation: Add the D3h A1-prime and E-prime branches with a conventional hexagonal cell. The note identifies the preset as a plane-wave Jones example and uses monolayer irrep names.
blocks.why: Bulk-like A1g/E2g names appearing in a reference passage must not replace the correct monolayer D3h labels in the material library.
blocks.check: The preset is MoS2-1L, not a bulk D6h material. Its coefficients remain illustrative.

blocks.title: Extend the library with graphene
blocks.explanation: Add a monolayer D6h G-mode example mapped to E2g. Supply the conventional hexagonal metric and a note that neither electronic bands nor vortex intensity are inferred.
blocks.why: A known Raman irrep is sufficient to demonstrate a polarization contraction, but not sufficient to compute all microscopic optical transitions.
blocks.check: The G family retains both E2g partners and their shared branch coefficient.

blocks.title: Extend the library with monoclinic 1T-prime MoTe2
blocks.explanation: Add C2h Ag and Bg in the unique-y convention, using an illustrative monoclinic β angle of 100 degrees. The note distinguishes the chosen inputs from measured fit parameters in the cited figure.
blocks.why: Nonorthogonal crystallographic axes require the lattice metric, while the tensor remains expressed in an orthonormal Cartesian frame.
blocks.check: The monoclinic Ag template contains an allowed xz entry; it is not forced into an orthorhombic diagonal tensor.

blocks.title: Extend the library with ReSe2
blocks.explanation: Add a Ci Ag example in Cartesian tensor axes, with an illustrative metric and a note requiring measured triclinic cell parameters and mode-specific coefficients for a sample calculation.
blocks.why: A fully populated symmetric tensor is allowed by Ci. A material dropdown alone cannot determine its orientation, principal axes or numerical coefficients.
blocks.check: The full Ci Ag family exposes all six independent symmetric entries.

blocks.title: default_paper_parameters: keep controls explicit
blocks.explanation: Return circular-rule defaults for the CIRCULAR workflow: s_in=+1, N=2, zero incident OAM, one zero phonon charge, no absorption charge and unestablished thin-2D assumptions. Linear and cubic workflows receive a zero scan-angle offset. Other workflows receive no paper-parameter dictionary here.
blocks.why: A workflow should not inherit another reference calculation merely because a hidden control retains an old value.
blocks.check: The general pipeline later merges these defaults with explicitly supplied active parameters. The assumptions checkbox is false by default.

blocks.title: paper_demo_config: build a declared reference workflow
blocks.explanation: Validate the requested CIRCULAR or LINEAR method, obtain a material demonstration configuration and replace its workflow policy with a coherent full-tensor rule and the selected direct circular-linear or paired-linear optical profile. Add explicit reference and illustrative-input notes.
blocks.why: The tensor library and scattering engine remain shared, while the reference-specific input set remains inspectable. Creating a demonstration does not certify its coefficients as measured material constants.
blocks.check: A LINEAR demonstration uses LINEAR_PAIR; a CIRCULAR demonstration uses CIRCULAR_LINEAR. Both retain coherent complete phonon tensors.

blocks.title: linear_bp_reference_config: enter published example ratios
blocks.explanation: Load the BP linear example, choose the declared normal side and enter separate Ag ratios c/a=1.96 with zero relative phase and c/a=1.32 with 94-degree relative phase. Enter the off-diagonal branch reference magnitude 1.30. The library xz coefficient is e even though the review names that entry f.
blocks.why: Reproducing a reference formula requires its coefficient ratio, phase, plane and angle convention, not only the material name or a visually similar curve.
blocks.check: The examples reproduce the stated coherent Eq. 13 convention; they are not digitized fits to all experimental points. The global a=1 scale is arbitrary for each illustrative branch.

blocks.title: circular_mos2_reference_config: declare the plane-wave example
blocks.explanation: Load the monolayer circular-channel example, label its intensity model as ell_i=0 and set the cyclic order to 3 with phonon charges 0,+2,-2. Mark the reference assumptions as declared for this example.
blocks.why: The polarization contractions demonstrate A1-prime and E-prime channels while the charge list supports a separate necessary-congruence diagnostic.
blocks.check: Changing an OAM charge later affects the rule check only; it does not turn the plane-wave intensity into a quantitative vortex calculation.

blocks.title: circular_integer: require true integer charges
blocks.explanation: Reject Python and NumPy Booleans, require a finite real scalar and verify that converting it to int does not change its value. Return that integer.
blocks.why: Modulo-N angular-momentum conditions are defined for integer charges. Accepting True as 1 or truncating 1.5 to 1 would silently change a selection-rule input.
blocks.check: 2 and 2.0 are accepted; True and 1.5 are rejected.

blocks.title: circular_congruence: validate the discrete rule inputs
blocks.explanation: Validate N and incident/scattered circular labels as integers. Restrict N to the implemented 2,3,4,6 orders and the two circular labels to +/-1. Validate incident OAM and require at least one integer phonon charge.
blocks.why: The congruence is a discrete symmetry condition under the assumptions of the reference. Invalid labels cannot be interpreted as an elliptical state or rounded into a valid charge.
blocks.check: A missing phonon-charge list or an unsupported cyclic order gives an error before a pass/fail statement is generated.

blocks.title: circular_congruence: test necessary conservation and absorption
blocks.explanation: For each phonon charge q, test (s_s-s_i-ell_i+q) mod N=0. If an electronic absorption charge difference is supplied, also test (delta_m-s_i-ell_i) mod N=0. Return matching charges, both pass indicators and whether absorption was actually checked.
blocks.why: A conservation congruence can pass while an optical subprocess is forbidden or an assumed symmetry axis is absent. The output therefore records necessary conditions instead of claiming an intensity or a sufficient scattering rule.
blocks.check: If absorption_delta_m is omitted, combined_necessary_pass is None rather than a fabricated complete pass. Each phonon charge is tested separately.

blocks.title: circular_basis_matrix: change the optical basis
blocks.explanation: Build U with σ⁺ and σ⁻ as columns and return U.H*R_perp*U. Rows correspond to the outgoing circular basis and columns to the incident circular basis.
blocks.why: Changing basis is a representation change of the same tensor contraction, not a new material response or a different intensity prescription.
blocks.check: The circular-basis amplitude for transformed states must equal the original Cartesian-basis amplitude. The Hermitian transpose is required because U is complex unitary.

blocks.title: circular_diagnostics: keep rules and intensities separate
blocks.explanation: Read the explicit paper parameters, copy them into a diagnostic record and state the plane-wave intensity scope. Independently test the necessary rule for both outgoing circular labels and append those results.
blocks.why: Requested vortex charge must not silently mask or rescale a plane-wave Jones curve. The user needs to see which assumptions were declared and which rules were actually evaluated.
blocks.check: The scope says whether thin-2D/electronic assumptions were declared. The selected intensity arrays are not modified by this function.

blocks.title: Compute complete circular channel matrices and powers
blocks.explanation: For each selected mode, transform every production term R_perp into the circular basis, substitute the same coefficient values and accumulate absolute-squared matrix entries over the declared partner tensors. Save the matrices, powers and row/column labels.
blocks.why: This gives all four circular input/output channels from the same tensor used elsewhere and preserves the distinction between within-tensor amplitude interference and partner-power addition.
blocks.check: For a single term, each matrix entry is one complete circular amplitude. Matrix element phases remain available separately from the tabulated powers.

blocks.title: Check the cyclic axis for orthorhombic and monoclinic settings
blocks.explanation: Inspect the actual Cartesian Z column of T. D2/D2h require a principal Cartesian normal and N=2. C2v uses its unique z C2 axis; C2/C2h use the unique y axis. Save compatibility and its convention note.
blocks.why: A tilted (211) surface normal in D2h is not automatically a twofold rotation axis. Selecting N=2 in a dropdown does not create that symmetry about the beam direction.
blocks.check: An orthorhombic principal-axis orientation can pass this axis check; a general tilted normal does not receive an extinction prediction from it.

blocks.title: Check higher cyclic axes or report uncertified cases
blocks.explanation: For supported trigonal, tetragonal and hexagonal settings, require Z along crystallographic z and an order dividing the implemented principal rotation order. Other groups receive an explicit unknown/uncertified axis record.
blocks.why: The reference rule depends on an actual cyclic symmetry operation about the chosen axis. The program must not infer that operation from a generic hkl label alone.
blocks.check: A compatible basal normal in a D3 setting supports order 3; a tilted normal does not. Unknown axis certification is not a proof that physical scattering is forbidden.

blocks.title: State the final applicability scope
blocks.explanation: Mark the rule applicable only when the declared thin-2D assumptions and cyclic-axis compatibility are both true. If the axis is incompatible, replace the scope message with a formal-congruence-only statement and return the diagnostic record.
blocks.why: A formal congruence result has a narrower meaning than a physically established extinction rule. Explicit scope prevents a bulk tilted-crystal example from being overinterpreted.
blocks.check: Passing eq24_pass alone must not override rule_applicable=False.

blocks.title: resonance_element: validate supplied energy inputs
blocks.explanation: Convert the laser-energy grid to a NumPy array, validate a nonnegative phonon energy and require finite excitation energies. Initialize a complex result array with the same shape.
blocks.why: This utility evaluates a supplied finite resonance sum. Symmetry, a band-gap number or a material label does not provide the missing microscopic matrix elements.
blocks.check: All energies and damping parameters must use the same unit; the function interface names eV. No resonance terms produces a zero supplied-term sum.

blocks.title: Evaluate complex third-order resonance denominators
blocks.explanation: For each supplied contribution, read the two transition energies, two positive damping values and a finite complex numerator weight. Add weight/[(E_L-Ecv+i*Gamma_c)*(E_L-Ephonon-Ecprime_v+i*Gamma_cprime)] to the result and return the complex array.
blocks.why: Finite damping regularizes resonance denominators and complex weights allow phase-sensitive interference between supplied terms. These values represent external microscopic input rather than a prediction from the tensor library.
blocks.check: The returned object is a complex response element versus excitation energy, not its squared intensity. Relative phase among contributions can change both its magnitude and argument.

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–8 in order and confirm the Cell 08/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: The source circular rule is a necessary condition with assumptions; it is not a general quantitative vortex intensity model.
N=2 congruence alone often cannot distinguish circular channels and cannot replace the tensor calculation.
The layer-plane and axis conventions must match the reference equations before interpreting a VV/VH comparison.
The resonance utility requires supplied energies, broadenings and complex numerator weights; these are not inferred from the material dropdown.

overview: Independent audits test the Jones states and complete-tensor interference without changing the selected calculation.
workflow: Sample exact fields on the angle grid.
Classify their sample polarization with normalized Stokes parameters.
Transform input and detector fields into crystal coordinates and reconstruct entry amplitudes independently.
Separate entry self-powers from coherent within-phonon interference.
Attach and report audit evidence with an explicit numerical-error bound.

blocks.title: Scope of this code section
blocks.explanation:
Independent polarization-state and within-mode interference diagnostics.

The diagnostics do not choose coefficients, align a polar plot, or replace
the selected intensity curve. They make the consequences of that selection
visible and test the coherent result by a second, entry-wise calculation.
blocks.why: This module-level documentation identifies the responsibility of the following definitions and prevents confusing reference/report helpers with the active calculation engine.
blocks.check: Documentation does not execute a calculation or select coefficients.

blocks.title: PAPER_EQUATION_MAP — Attach equation provenance
blocks.explanation: The text maps complex-response tensor contraction and phase interference to DOI 10.1039/D1CP03626B, and the conditional circular rule to DOI 10.1039/D1CP02209A. It is report metadata, not an input to an intensity formula.
blocks.why: A checking program should state which physical claim each source supports. A selection-rule reference cannot be used as a numerical intensity formula.
blocks.check: Changing prose here must not change a calculated curve.

blocks.title: vector_samples — Evaluate an exact field on the angular grid
blocks.explanation: First convert the angle input into a floating NumPy array. For each symbolic field component, lambdify creates a NumPy evaluator; broadcast_to also expands an angle-independent scalar into a full angular row. vstack then returns a dimension-by-angle complex array. The final finite-value test rejects an invalid numerical field.
blocks.why: Independent audits need all field components in the same array shape even when a circular state is constant. Keeping dtype=complex preserves phase and makes conjugate products reliable.
blocks.check: A fixed two-component circular vector should return a 2-by-N array with identical columns, and a rotating real analyzer should return two angle-dependent rows.

blocks.title: normalized_stokes — Classify the actual polarization state
blocks.explanation: The function reshapes one field into two components and obtains its norm with vdot, which conjugates the first vector. It then evaluates S1=(|Ex|²−|Ey|²)/S0, S2=2Re(Ex*Ey)/S0 and S3=2Im(Ex*Ey)/S0. A tolerance identifies circular, linear or intermediate elliptical states.
blocks.why: A menu label is insufficient to establish the physical polarization at the sample. Stokes parameters inspect the actual complex vector. The sign convention for S3 and the time dependence are stated rather than silently assigning an LCP/RCP name.
blocks.check: For σ⁺=(1,i)/sqrt(2), S3 is +1 in this fixed laboratory basis; for a real nonzero linear state S3 is zero.

blocks.title: optical_state_audit — Trace incident and detection states back to the sample
blocks.explanation: At scan angles 0, 45 and 90 degrees, vector_samples evaluates Ein and effective_analyzer. Each column is passed to normalized_stokes. With ki=−Z and ks=+Z, the recorded propagation-relative expectations are −S3 for the incoming state and +S3 for the outgoing state. The returned record also retains B and both exact fields.
blocks.why: A linear analyzer after a return waveplate is generally an elliptical detection state when viewed at the sample. This audit prevents interpreting the analyzer hardware label as the sample polarization.
blocks.check: Compare the effective detection S3 values of QWP and CUBIC_SIGMA at intermediate angles; equal circular endpoints do not establish equal scans.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Prepare independent crystal-frame field samples
blocks.explanation: The audit transforms the actual input and effective detection vectors into crystal coordinates, evaluates every nonzero Cartesian tensor entry, adds the resulting amplitudes within each complete phonon tensor, and only then adds powers over orthogonal phonon partners. Entry self-powers are stored separately. Their difference from the coherent result is the signed within-mode interference. A propagated roundoff bound protects exact dark channels without changing a curve. The audit caches incident and effective detector samples by optical profile. For a crystal, T*P.T embeds each transverse state in crystal coordinates; the 2D source uses its two-component fields directly.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-partner handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Add entry amplitudes inside each complete tensor
blocks.explanation: For every orthogonal partner, detection[row]* is multiplied by R[row,column] and incident[column]. The entry amplitudes are added before abs(amplitude)**2. Separately accumulated abs(entry)**2 terms provide the self-power diagnostic; coherent−self_power reveals all within-partner cross terms.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-partner handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Handle a dark-channel cancellation without altering intensity
blocks.explanation: The code estimates amplitude roundoff from uncancelled self-powers, propagates it into a power error bound, and combines it with a relative tolerance. This avoids dividing a cancellation residue by an almost-zero intensity. An actual mismatching coherent result raises ArithmeticError.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-partner handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Return complete audit arrays and their interpretation
blocks.explanation: The record retains the independently reconstructed coherent intensity, self-powers, signed interference, selected result, individual entry amplitudes, labels and error bounds. It explicitly says that component self-powers depend on the chosen basis, whereas the complete coherent result does not.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-partner handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: attach_physics_audit — Attach audit evidence without replacing results
blocks.explanation: For each optical profile, the function stores a sample-state audit. It calls tensor_interference_audit and records whether the selected calculation uses a coherent complete tensor or the explicit legacy component prescription. The run is returned with a new physics field; its calculated arrays remain untouched.
blocks.why: Diagnostics must explain or test a result rather than silently correcting it to a preferred plot. Separating audit data also makes exports reproducible.
blocks.check: The intensity arrays before and after this function should be equal; only additional physics metadata should appear.

blocks.title: physics_audit_markdown — Present polarization and interference checks
blocks.explanation: The reporter reads the audit record, displays the effective detection vector, and builds tables of polarization type and S3 at representative angles. It explains the laboratory-basis versus beam-direction convention and tabulates entry self-powers, interference, coherent intensity and the selected curve. Separate notes identify the source model and the legacy component prescription when applicable.
blocks.why: The reader needs to know what is being added as amplitudes and what is being added as powers. The tables make constructive and destructive interference visible and disclose the model scope.
blocks.check: A negative interference term is permitted, but the final measured-model intensity remains nonnegative. The reporter does not modify run["curves"].

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–9 in order and confirm the Cell 09/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: The analyzer after a return waveplate is not generally the same Jones state as its linear transmission axis at the detector.
Same laboratory circular basis labels are not automatically same propagation-relative helicities in backscattering.
Tensor-entry self-powers are basis-dependent diagnostics; only the complete coherent intensity is invariant.

overview: This cell is the production coordinator: it validates physical inputs, calculates with the common 3D Jones engine, and adds the separate Ag presentation channels.
workflow: Construct a fully declared configuration.
Check the metric, frame, coefficients and optical policy.
Select complete symmetry tensors and orthogonal partners.
Calculate complex amplitudes and powers on a common grid.
Attach independent physical checks.
Calculate separate Ag tensor contributions using that same engine.
Retain complete-mode audits and symbolic/basis-equivalence evidence.

blocks.title: Scope of this code section
blocks.explanation: One physical-input contract and separate Cartesian Ag presentation channels.
blocks.why: This module-level documentation identifies the responsibility of the following definitions and prevents confusing reference/report helpers with the active calculation engine.
blocks.check: Documentation does not execute a calculation or select coefficients.

blocks.title: validate_lattice_for_group — Check the cell metric against the tensor convention
blocks.explanation: The six lattice parameters are converted into a finite numerical array. The selected crystal system determines the allowed conventional cell relations: orthorhombic right angles; a=b for tetragonal; a=b=c for cubic; conventional hexagonal a=b and γ=120 degrees for the trigonal/hexagonal settings; and α=γ=90 degrees for unique-y monoclinic tensors.
blocks.why: The tensor library uses explicit Cartesian axis conventions. Mixing a tensor setting with incompatible cell angles or primitive indices would rotate the wrong physical normal, even if the matrix multiplication itself is valid.
blocks.check: A cubic preset with unequal a0,b0,c0 must be rejected. A general custom tensor is not forced into a named symmetry metric.

blocks.title: demonstration_config — Construct an illustrative, fully declared experiment
blocks.explanation: The function resolves a material preset, obtains its tensor definitions and surface preset, and returns a configuration dictionary. It supplies each branch with its own coefficient dictionary, lattice, hkl, uvw, normal side, azimuth, optical profile, scan grid and display options. The historical workflow label and Ag rule are explicitly recorded.
blocks.why: One complete input record is the reproducibility contract for every later calculation. The defaults are demonstrations; they are not a prediction of a material’s unknown Raman coefficients.
blocks.check: Inspect the returned dictionary without running a calculation. Changing a preset must not be confused with experimentally determining its coefficients or lattice ratios.

blocks.title: component_reference_config — Declare the legacy slide-prescription regression case
blocks.explanation: Starting from the CaNb2O6 reference optics, the function inserts the explicit unity-metric slide frame and restricts the selected mode to Ag. Its note and direct-state parameters identify θᵢ=45 degrees, βᵢ=90 degrees, θₛ₀=45 degrees and βₛ=90 degrees.
blocks.why: The old component-power prescription needs a named reference configuration so it can be checked without becoming the general material rule.
blocks.check: This function is a historical regression input. The edition-14 main interface instead starts from slide_component_config and plots the Ag contributions separately.

blocks.title: qwp_source_config — Create the original effective optical-source model
blocks.explanation: The returned dictionary chooses QWP_SOURCE_2D, the QWP chain and real source amplitudes a,A with δ,φ supplied in degrees. It explicitly has no material, point group or crystal-orientation input. The original source uses one complete coherent tensor.
blocks.why: An effective two-dimensional source tensor is a reference optical model, not a symmetry assignment to an orthorhombic crystal. Its crystal-independent status must be visible.
blocks.check: Selecting this model should make crystal orientation inactive; a surface label cannot change its output.

blocks.title: physical_start_config — Provide a principal-surface 3D QWP example
blocks.explanation: The function starts from the CaNb2O6 QWP preset and selects (100) with [010] in-plane. It labels the example as a coherent 3D extension and states that coefficients are illustrative.
blocks.why: A principal orthorhombic surface permits an uncomplicated test of the 3D tensor/QWP calculation without assuming the length ratios needed for a tilted surface.
blocks.check: For this (100) example, changing the positive lattice lengths without changing the axis convention does not tilt the reciprocal normal away from crystal x.

blocks.title: validate_method_policy — Validate the shared general-model contract
blocks.explanation: This validator checks the method/model labels and their allowed optical profiles. GENERAL requires a full crystal tensor and retains coherent complete-mode amplitudes; the separate Cartesian display is not its physical intensity rule. Historical QWP, component-reference, circular, linear and cubic routes retain their own declared rules and required parameters. The method and tensor-model keys are validated first. The GENERAL branch requires CRYSTAL_3D and a declared optical profile, enforces a coherent complete-mode tensor and merges explicit paper/control defaults.
blocks.why: The same low-level multiplication can be used by several experiments, but an accidental mixture of a reference intensity prescription and another optical chain is not a valid new experiment. Invalid hybrids are rejected rather than guessed.
blocks.check: A GENERAL calculation requesting a component-power-sum complete-mode rule must fail. A QWP_SOURCE_2D model cannot silently become a crystal calculation.

blocks.title: validate_method_policy — Validate historical routes without combining their rules
blocks.explanation: QWP and the component-reference prescription receive distinct allowed chains and Ag rules. Circular, linear and cubic workflows validate their own profile lists. A conflicting Ag rule is rejected, and irrelevant paper parameters are removed from older routes.
blocks.why: The same low-level multiplication can be used by several experiments, but an accidental mixture of a reference intensity prescription and another optical chain is not a valid new experiment. Invalid hybrids are rejected rather than guessed.
blocks.check: A GENERAL calculation requesting a component-power-sum complete-mode rule must fail. A QWP_SOURCE_2D model cannot silently become a crystal calculation.

blocks.title: assemble_calculated_run — Calculate records, arrays and exact harmonic summaries
blocks.explanation: A common linspace creates the angular samples. For each family, record_builder computes amplitudes from the already-selected tensors and optics; evaluate_terms produces arrays and harmonic summaries. Complete circular-channel projections are also evaluated. The returned run stores inputs, geometry, families, terms, curves, summaries and the correct scan label. The angular grid is shared. For each family, record_builder applies the tensor to its actual optics and evaluate_terms computes amplitudes, partner powers, the requested total and continuous extrema.
